entries.definition: The number produced by division.
To mention a source formally, especially in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 正式提到一个来源，尤指在写作中。

entries.definition: To say or do something again.
To give an approximate figure in advance.
To set the amount of money asked for something.

normalIntro.en: The word marks a passage or a price: both are figures set out for others to read, repeat or accept.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词标记一段话或一个价格：两者都是摆出来供别人阅读、重复或接受的数字。

normal.en: Quote is a shortened quotation, so the noun and the verb look exactly alike.
normal.cn: quote 是 quotation 的缩略，所以名词和动词长得一模一样。

normal.en: Quote unquote is the spoken way of putting quotation marks around someone else's phrase.
normal.cn: quote unquote 是口语中给别人的说法加上引号的方式。

normal.en: A builder's quote is a price marked on paper, using the same verb as quoting a sentence.
normal.cn: 施工方的 quote 是写在纸上的价格，用的动词与引用一句话相同。

normal.en: To quote someone on a subject is to report their exact words about it.
normal.cn: quote someone on 某话题，就是报告他们对这个话题的原话。

normal.en: Misquote means to get the words wrong, and it is one of the commonest complaints in journalism.
normal.cn: misquote 意为引错话，是新闻业最常见的投诉之一。

abstract.en: To quote well is to disappear for a moment and let the other voice be heard clearly.
abstract.cn: 引得好，就是让自己暂时消失，让另一个声音被清楚地听见。

abstract.en: A price quoted in advance is a promise about the future, which is why a quote can feel like a commitment.
abstract.cn: 预先报出的价格是对未来的一个承诺，所以 quote 会让人觉得像一种约定。

abstract.en: Quoting and pricing both fix a number in place, one on a page and one on a market.
abstract.cn: 引用与定价都是把一个数字固定下来，一个固定在纸页上，一个固定在市场上。

examples.en: She quoted the contract exactly in her letter.
examples.cn: 她在信里一字不差地引用了合同。

examples.en: The shop quoted me a lower price for the same chair.
examples.cn: 同一把椅子，这家店给我报的价更低。

examples.en: He wrote the coach's quote on a card above his desk.
examples.cn: 他把教练的那句话写在一张卡片上，贴到书桌上方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阔特」——阔气地把别人的话原样搬来，记得标出处，记住 quote 是引用。

root: 拉丁语 quot（多少）→ 中世纪拉丁语 quotare（编号、标记）→ 古法语 quoter → 英语 quote；同族有 quotation、quota、quotient。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a marked figure; the senses divide into repeating words, setting a price, the repeated words themselves and the price itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被标出的数字或段落」；义项分为重复他人的话、定出价格、被重复的话本身，以及价格本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a recorder wound back to the start, beside a word-for-word transcript.
core.cn: 核心意象：倒回开头的录音笔，旁边放着逐字对照的文稿。

branches.en: a finger tracing one line twice
branches.cn: 手指把一行字描了两遍

branches.en: a figure written on an order form
branches.cn: 写在订单上的一个数字

branches.en: a sentence framed on a wall
branches.cn: 被框起来挂在墙上的一句话

branches.en: a sum circled at the bottom of a letter
branches.cn: 信末被圈出的金额

branches.en: the act of quoting and the thing quoted
branches.cn: 引用的动作与被引用之物

intro.en: The word is a shortened French borrowing on the Latin root of numbering, with English endings that build nouns, adjectives and negative verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「编号」词根上的法语缩略借词，加上构成名词、形容词与否定动词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem quot- also gave quota and quotient, which keep the plain idea of a counted share.
latinIntro.cn: quot- 这个词干还给出了 quota 与 quotient，它们保留了「被计算出的份额」这一朴素意思。

definition_zh: 赛跑；竞赛；种族；急奔；（磨坊）水道
definition_en: a competition to see who is fastest; a contest between people or groups; a group of people sharing ancestry; to move very fast; a channel of water leading to a mill
core_image: 傍晚的跑道上，几名选手同时冲过起跑线
scene: 傍晚的跑道上，发令枪响后几名选手同时冲出起跑线。He won the final race by less than a second.
sceneCN: 这里 race 是「赛跑、竞速比赛」（第 1 个义项：比谁跑得快的比赛）；句意为他以不到一秒的优势赢下了最后一场比赛。画面里可留意：起点线、发令枪、几乎并排的身影。

pos.zh: 赛跑；竞赛；种族；（磨坊）水道
急速行进；参赛；使拼命跑

derivatives.zh: race 加 -er，指参赛者或赛车
race 加 -ing，指赛跑、赛车等竞技活动
race 加 -ial，指与种族有关的
race 加 -ist，指持种族歧视观点的

senses.title: A competition of speed
senses.definition: a contest to find who or what is fastest
senses.definitionCN: 比出谁或什么最快的一种竞赛
senses.example: He won the hundred-metre race.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢下了百米赛跑。
senses.why: The contest sense comes from an old northern word for a rush or a run, so the word began as the movement itself.
senses.whyCN: 比赛义来自一个古老的北方词，意为「急冲、奔跑」，所以这个词最初指的就是那股奔跑。

senses.title: A contest between people or groups
senses.definition: a situation in which people or groups try to be first to reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体争相抢先达到某个目标的情形
senses.example: The race for the contract ended in a tie.
senses.exampleCN: 争取这份合同的竞争以平局收场。
senses.why: Once a race was a run toward a line, any struggle to arrive first could be called a race, even without running.
senses.whyCN: 当 race 指朝终点线奔跑之后，任何「抢在前头」的争夺都可以叫 race，即使根本不用跑。

senses.title: A group sharing ancestry
senses.definition: a group of people regarded as sharing ancestry and physical features, a term used with care
senses.definitionCN: 被视为共享血统与外貌特征的一群人，此词使用时须谨慎
senses.example: People of every race took part in the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 各种族的人都参加了这项调查。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different source, an Italian word for kind or breed, and its scientific status has been much debated.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来源不同，出自一个意为「种类、品种」的意大利语词，其科学地位一直备受争议。

senses.title: To move very fast
senses.definition: to move at great speed, often in a hurry or in competition
senses.definitionCN: 以很快的速度移动，常带匆忙或竞争意味
senses.example: She raced to catch the last bus.
senses.exampleCN: 她飞奔去赶末班车。
senses.why: Since the word first named a rush, the verb simply describes the act of rushing, with or without a contest.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词最初指一股急冲，动词就只是描述急冲这一动作，无论有没有比赛。

senses.title: A channel of water
senses.definition: a fast current of water, especially one made to drive a mill wheel
senses.definitionCN: 流速较快的水道，尤指为驱动磨坊水轮而开的渠道
senses.example: The old mill still stands beside the race.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老磨坊仍然立在水道旁边。
senses.why: Water rushing through a narrow channel moves like a runner, so the old sense of a rush survived in the mill race.
senses.whyCN: 水冲过窄渠时像奔跑者一样急行，于是「急冲」这一古老意思在磨坊水道里保留下来。

intro.en: Race is really two words: the contest sense comes from an old northern word for a rush, while the ancestry sense comes through French and Italian from a word of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: race 实际上是两个词：比赛义来自古老的北方词「急冲」，而种族义经法语与意大利语来自一个来源不确定的词。

items.en: Ras meant a running or a rush, and it entered northern English with the sense of swift movement.
items.cn: ras 意为奔跑、急冲，带着快速运动的意思进入英格兰北部英语。

items.en: Middle English race named a run or a course, and from that a contest of speed.
items.cn: 中古英语的 race 指一次奔跑或一段跑道，由此生出速度竞赛之义。

items.en: A separate French word razza, of uncertain origin, meant a breed or a kind, especially of animals.
items.cn: 另一个来源不确定的法语词 razza 意为品种或种类，尤指动物的品种。

items.en: English applied the breed sense to groups of people, a use that later became scientifically and socially disputed.
items.cn: 英语把「品种」义用到人群上，这一用法后来在科学与社会层面都引发争议。

items.en: Modern English keeps both words: race as a contest and race as a category of people, plus the mill race of flowing water.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了两个词：作为竞赛的 race、作为人群类别的 race，以及指流水渠道的磨坊 race。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the word; the near-meaning group gathers words for contests, speed and ancestry.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个词构成的形式；近义组收表示竞赛、速度与血统的词。

entries.definition: A person or vehicle that takes part in races.
The sport of competing for speed.
Connected with a group sharing ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 与共享血统的群体有关的。

entries.definition: Someone who treats people unequally because of their group.
entries.definitionCN: 因所属群体而区别对待他人的人。

entries.definition: A competition in which people try to win.
The activity of trying to do better than others.
To run at top speed for a short distance.
Belonging to a group with shared culture and origin.
entries.definitionCN: 属于共享文化与来源的群体。

normalIntro.en: The contest sense grew from a word for a rush of movement, and the ancestry sense grew from a word for breed; English keeps both under one spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 比赛义从表示「急冲」的词生长出来，种族义从表示「品种」的词生长出来；英语把两者放在同一个拼写之下。

normal.en: Race as a contest and race as a category of people have different origins that happen to share one spelling.
normal.cn: 作为竞赛的 race 与作为人群类别的 race 来源不同，只是碰巧共用同一个拼写。

normal.en: A race against time is a race with no competitor but the clock.
normal.cn: race against time 是没有对手、只与时钟赛跑的比赛。

normal.en: Racer, racing and racial all come from the same short word with different endings.
normal.cn: racer、racing、racial 都是同一个短词加上不同词尾。

normal.en: A mill race is water rushing through a channel, which shows how old the sense of a rush really is.
normal.cn: mill race 指冲过渠道的水，可见「急冲」这一古老意思有多深。

normal.en: The human race uses race in the broad sense of all people together, not in the sense of a category.
normal.cn: the human race 用的是「全人类」这一宽泛义，而不是「某一类别」义。

abstract.en: Sorting people into races says more about the sorter than about the people being sorted.
abstract.cn: 把人分成种族，更多说明分类者本身，而不是被分类的人。

abstract.en: A race is exciting because everyone agrees on the same finish line, which is also why disagreements about the line are so bitter.
abstract.cn: 比赛令人兴奋，因为大家认同同一条终点线，这也正是关于终点线的分歧如此激烈的原因。

abstract.en: Speed is easy to measure and easy to admire, which is why so much of modern life is arranged as a race.
abstract.cn: 速度容易测量，也容易赞美，所以现代生活有很大一部分被安排成一场比赛。

examples.en: She came second in the school race.
examples.cn: 她在学校赛跑中得了第二。

examples.en: The two companies are in a race to launch first.
examples.cn: 两家公司在争抢谁先发布。

examples.en: He raced down the stairs when he heard the alarm.
examples.cn: 听到警报，他飞奔下楼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐丝」——像一根锐利的丝线划过终点，速度极快，记住 race 是赛跑、竞赛。

root: 比赛义源于古诺斯语 ras（奔跑、急冲）；种族义经法语与意大利语来自 razza（品种，来源不确定）；两词在英语中同形。同族有 racer、racing、racial。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a rush; one branch runs from rush to contest, the other from breed to ancestry, and a third survives in the channel of a mill.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「急冲」；一条支线从急冲走到竞赛，另一条从品种走到血统，还有一条留在磨坊的水道里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: runners leaving the start line together on an evening track.
core.cn: 核心意象：傍晚跑道上同时冲出起跑线的选手。

branches.en: a gun fired beside a track
branches.cn: 跑道旁打响的发令枪

branches.en: two firms chasing one contract
branches.cn: 两家公司争抢同一份合同

branches.en: a form asking for ancestry
branches.cn: 要求填写血统的表格

branches.en: feet taking the stairs three at a time
branches.cn: 一步三级地冲下楼梯

branches.en: the same rush, once on legs and once in a mill channel
branches.cn: 同一种急冲，一次靠双腿，一次在磨坊渠道里

intro.en: The contest word is native and northern, the ancestry word came through French and Italian, and English adds its usual endings to both.
intro.cn: 表示竞赛的词是本族词，来自北方；表示血统的词经法语和意大利语传来；英语给两者加上了惯用的词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for either word.
latinIntro.cn: 这两个来源都没有可靠的拉丁语出处记录。

definition_zh: 根本的；彻底的；激进的；激进分子；根式
definition_en: relating to the root of a matter and therefore thorough; wanting great political or social change; a person who wants such change; a root expression in mathematics
core_image: 一棵被连根拔起的树，根须上还挂着泥土
scene: 会议室里，有人把一份厚厚的改革方案摊开，主张从制度本身动手。The committee proposed radical changes to the way the city collects waste.
sceneCN: 这里 radical 是「根本的、彻底的」（第 1 个义项：触及事物根基因而彻底的）；句意为委员会提议对城市收运垃圾的方式进行彻底改革。画面里可留意：摊开的厚方案、被翻到卷边的页角。

pos.zh: 根本的；彻底的；激进的；根生的
激进分子；（数学）根式；（语言）词根

derivatives.zh: radical 加 -ly，指从根本上、彻底地
radical 加 -ism，指主张彻底变革的激进主义
radical 加 -ize，指使某人变得激进

senses.title: Relating to the root of a matter
senses.definition: touching the root or foundation of a problem, and therefore thorough
senses.definitionCN: 触及问题的根源或基础，因而十分彻底
senses.example: The plan calls for radical changes in the tax system.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划要求对税制进行彻底改革。
senses.why: Latin radix meant a root, and radicalis meant belonging to a root, so a radical change goes down to the root of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 radix 意为根，radicalis 意为属于根的，因此 radical change 就是深入到事物根部的改变。

senses.title: Wanting great political change
senses.definition: favouring far-reaching change in politics or society, often by rapid means
senses.definitionCN: 主张在政治或社会上进行影响深远的改变，常指以较快手段实现
senses.example: The party's radical wing wants to abolish the old rules.
senses.exampleCN: 该党的激进派想废除旧规则。
senses.why: A reformer who wants to reach the root of a social problem is called radical, because the root is exactly what the word names.
senses.whyCN: 想触及社会问题根源的改革者被称为 radical，因为这个词命名的正是「根」。

senses.title: A person who wants such change
senses.definition: someone who holds radical political views and works for them
senses.definitionCN: 持激进政治观点并为之行动的人
senses.example: He was a radical in his youth and a moderate later.
senses.exampleCN: 他年轻时是激进分子，后来成了温和派。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for the person who carries the quality, a common path in English.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，用来指具有这种性质的人，这是英语里常见的路径。

senses.title: Growing from the root
senses.definition: growing from or near the root of a plant, as some leaves do
senses.definitionCN: 从植物根部或近根部生长，如某些叶子
senses.example: Radical leaves of this plant lie almost flat on the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物的根生叶几乎平贴在地面上。
senses.why: Botany kept the plain Latin sense: a part attached at the root is literally radical.
senses.whyCN: 植物学保留了拉丁语最朴素的意思：附着在根部的部分字面上就是 radical。

senses.title: A root expression in mathematics
senses.definition: a mathematical expression written with a root sign, or the sign itself
senses.definitionCN: 用根号写成的数学表达式，或根号本身
senses.example: Simplify the radical before you add the two terms.
senses.exampleCN: 先把根式化简，再把两项相加。
senses.why: Mathematics uses the root image directly: the radical sign points to the root of a number.
senses.whyCN: 数学直接使用「根」这一意象：根号所指的就是一个数的根。

intro.en: Radical comes from the Latin word for root and its adjective, and the sense of thoroughness grew from the picture of reaching down to the root.
intro.cn: radical 源自拉丁语表示根的名词及其形容词，而「彻底」这一层意思从「向下触及根部」的画面生长出来。

items.en: Radix meant the root of a plant and, figuratively, the base or origin of anything.
items.cn: radix 指植物的根，也比喻任何事物的基础或起源。

items.en: The genitive radicis, of a root, supplied the stem from which the adjective was formed.
items.cn: 属格 radicis（根的）提供了构成形容词的词干。

items.en: Radicalis meant belonging to a root, and it was used in grammar and medicine as well as in botany.
items.cn: radicalis 意为属于根的，除植物学外也用于语法与医学。

items.en: English took the word for what goes to the root of a matter, and politics gave it the sense of far-reaching change.
items.cn: 英语接受这个词，用来指触及事物根本的东西，政治又赋予它「影响深远之变革」的意思。

items.en: Modern English keeps the senses of root cause, political extreme, root growth and the root sign in algebra.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了根本原因、政治上的极端、根部生长，以及代数中的根号这几层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin stem of root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of depth and extremes.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「根」词干上的词；近义组收表示深入与极端的形容词。

entries.definition: A small red root vegetable eaten raw.
To remove something completely, as if by pulling it out by the root.
entries.definitionCN: 像连根拔起那样彻底清除某物。

entries.definition: In a thorough or fundamental way.
The belief in far-reaching change.
Forming the base of something.
Extreme and severe in effect.
Far beyond the ordinary.
Complete in every detail.

normalIntro.en: The root is the picture: a change that goes to the root, a plant part at the root, and the root sign in algebra.
normalIntro.cn: 「根」就是这幅画面的核心：深入根部的改变、长在根部的植物部分，以及代数里的根号。

normal.en: Radical, radish and eradicate all share the Latin word for root, which makes the family easy to hold together.
normal.cn: radical、radish 与 eradicate 都共用拉丁语「根」一词，整族词因此很容易串在一起。

normal.en: A radical reform is not just a big reform; it is one that reaches the root of the system.
normal.cn: radical reform 不只是大改革，而是触及制度根基的改革。

normal.en: The radical sign in mathematics is shaped like a roof over a number, pointing back to its root.
normal.cn: 数学里的根号形状像一个盖在数字上的屋顶，指向它的根。

normal.en: Radical leaves grow at the base of the plant, which is the literal botanical sense.
normal.cn: radical leaves 长在植物基部，这正是植物学里的字面义。

normal.en: Radicalism is the noun for the belief, radicalize the verb for making someone hold it.
normal.cn: radicalism 是表示这种主张的名词，radicalize 是使某人接受它的动词。

abstract.en: To change something radically is to admit that the visible problem was only a symptom.
abstract.cn: 彻底改变某物，就是承认看得见的问题只是症状。

abstract.en: The same word can mean wise depth or dangerous haste, depending on who is describing the change.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可指有智慧的深刻，也可指危险的急躁，取决于谁在描述这场改变。

abstract.en: Everything grows from a root, so the word for root quietly honors what is usually invisible.
abstract.cn: 万物都从根部长出，因此「根」这个词也在悄悄致敬那些通常看不见的部分。

examples.en: The company needs radical changes, not small adjustments.
examples.cn: 这家公司需要彻底变革，而不是小修小补。

examples.en: His radical views made him unpopular with the board.
examples.cn: 他的激进观点使他不受董事会欢迎。

examples.en: In algebra, we first simplify the radical and then solve the equation.
examples.cn: 在代数里，我们先化简根式，再解方程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐的抠」——锐利地往根里抠，一直挖到最根本处，记住 radical 是根本的、激进的。

root: 拉丁语 radix（根）→ radicis（根的）→ 晚期拉丁语 radicalis（属于根的）→ 英语 radical；同族有 radish、eradicate、radically。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a root; the senses divide into a root-deep change, a political extreme, the person holding it, growth at the root and the root sign.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「根」；义项分为深入根源的改变、政治上的极端、持此立场的人、根部的生长，以及根号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tree pulled up by its roots, earth still clinging to them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵被连根拔起的树，根须上还挂着泥土。

branches.en: a knife cutting down to the base
branches.cn: 一直切到根基的一刀

branches.en: a speaker demanding a new order
branches.cn: 要求建立新秩序的发言者

branches.en: leaves lying flat at the stem base
branches.cn: 平贴茎基部的叶子

branches.en: a sign drawn over a number
branches.cn: 画在数字上方的符号

branches.en: the same depth, once in a repair and once in politics
branches.cn: 同一种深入，一次在修补中，一次在政治中

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin noun for root, its stem and adjective ending, with English endings for adverbs, beliefs and verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示根的名词、其词干与形容词词尾构成，再加上表示副词、主张与动词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem radic- is short but reaches English in several common words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干 radic- 很短，却在英语里伸进了好几个常用词。

definition_zh: 收音机；广播；无线电；用无线电发送
definition_en: a device that receives broadcast sound; the broadcasting of sound by radio waves; the technology of sending signals by electromagnetic waves; to send a message by radio
core_image: 一台老式收音机的指针停在刻度盘上，扬声器微微发亮
scene: 厨房里，老式收音机的指针在刻度上滑动，水壶的蒸汽把窗玻璃蒙上一层白雾。She turned the radio down when the phone rang.
sceneCN: 这里 radio 是「收音机」（第 1 个义项：接收广播声音的装置）；句意为电话响时她把收音机的声音调小了。画面里可留意：刻度盘上的指针、冒汽的水壶、蒙雾的窗。

pos.zh: 收音机；广播；无线电
用无线电发送；用无线电联络

derivatives.zh: radio 与 man 复合，指从事无线电通信工作的人
radio 与 controlled 复合，指靠无线电操纵的
radio- 与 isotope 复合，指具有放射性的同位素

senses.title: A receiving device
senses.definition: a piece of equipment that picks up broadcast sound and plays it
senses.definitionCN: 接收广播声音并播放出来的设备
senses.example: She turned on the radio in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她在厨房里打开了收音机。
senses.why: The device is named by shortening the technical word for wireless communication, so the machine carries the name of the method.
senses.whyCN: 这台设备的名字是「无线通信」这一技术词的缩略，因此机器承袭了方法的名字。

senses.title: Broadcasting by radio waves
senses.definition: the activity or service of sending sound to many listeners at once
senses.definitionCN: 把声音同时发送给许多听众的活动或服务
senses.example: The interview will be on the radio tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 这段采访今晚会在广播里播出。
senses.why: Once sound could travel without wires, broadcasting became a public service, and English called it simply the radio.
senses.whyCN: 声音既能不用电线传播，广播便成了公共服务，英语就径直称之为 the radio。

senses.title: Wireless communication technology
senses.definition: the technology of sending signals through space by electromagnetic waves
senses.definitionCN: 通过电磁波在空间中发送信号的技术
senses.example: The message was sent by radio from the ship.
senses.exampleCN: 这条消息是用船上的无线电发出的。
senses.why: This is the broadest sense: the physical method itself, used by ships, aircraft and stations alike.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽泛的一层：指这种物理方法本身，船只、飞机与电台都在使用。

senses.title: To send a message by radio
senses.definition: to communicate with someone by radio, especially in an emergency
senses.definitionCN: 用无线电与某人联络，尤指在紧急情况下
senses.example: The pilot radioed for help as the fog closed in.
senses.exampleCN: 雾合拢上来时，飞行员用无线电求救。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, naming the act of sending a message through the same technology.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词，指通过同一技术发送消息这一动作。

intro.en: Radio is a shortened form of words built on the Latin word for ray; the technology of wireless signalling took the name of the rays it uses.
intro.cn: radio 是建立在拉丁语表示射线的词之上的词语的缩略；无线通信技术采用了它所使用的那种射线的名字。

items.en: Radius meant a spoke or a ray, a straight line sent out from a centre.
items.cn: radius 指辐条或射线，即从中心射出的一条直线。

items.en: Radiare meant to send out rays, and the stem radi- entered scientific language as a combining form.
items.cn: radiare 意为发出射线，词干 radi- 作为构词成分进入科学语言。

items.en: Early wireless signalling was called radiotelegraphy, sending telegraph messages by electromagnetic waves.
items.cn: 早期的无线通信被称为 radiotelegraphy，即用电磁波发送电报。

items.en: English speakers shortened the long technical word to radio in the early twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，英语使用者把这个冗长的技术词缩略为 radio。

items.en: Modern English uses radio for the device, the broadcast service, the technology and the act of signalling.
items.cn: 现代英语用 radio 指设备、广播服务、技术以及发送信号的行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin stem of rays; the near-meaning group gathers words for broadcasting and wireless signalling.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「射线」词干上的词；近义组收表示广播与无线通信的词。

entries.definition: A detection system using reflected radio waves.
entries.definitionCN: 利用反射无线电波进行探测的系统。

entries.definition: A line from the centre of a circle to its edge.
entries.definitionCN: 从圆心到圆周的一条线。

entries.definition: Energy sent out as waves or particles.
entries.definitionCN: 以波或粒子形式发出的能量。

entries.definition: A person who works with radio equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 从事无线电设备工作的人。

entries.definition: To send sound or pictures to many receivers.
entries.definitionCN: 把声音或图像发送给许多接收者。

entries.definition: Working without connecting wires.
entries.definitionCN: 不通过连接导线工作的。

entries.definition: A device that picks up transmitted signals.
entries.definitionCN: 接收所传送信号的装置。

entries.definition: The sending out of signals or power.

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin ray in modern dress: wireless signalling was named after the rays that carry it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是穿上现代外衣的拉丁语「射线」：无线通信以承载它的射线命名。

normal.en: Radio, radius and radiation all begin with the Latin word for a ray leaving a centre.
normal.cn: radio、radius 与 radiation 都从拉丁语表示「从中心射出的射线」一词开始。

normal.en: On the radio names the service, while a radio names the box on the kitchen table.
normal.cn: on the radio 指广播服务，而 a radio 指厨房桌上的那台机器。

normal.en: Radio silence means no signals are being sent, often by a ship or an aircraft that must stay unheard.
normal.cn: radio silence 指不发送任何信号，常是船只或飞机必须保持静默时。

normal.en: To radio someone is to send a message by radio rather than by phone.
normal.cn: to radio 某人就是用无线电而不是电话发送消息。

normal.en: Radar is radio detection and ranging, a child of the same technology.
normal.cn: radar 是无线电探测与测距，是同一技术的产物。

abstract.en: Radio made a voice present in millions of rooms at once, the first everyday experience of shared listening.
abstract.cn: 广播让一个声音同时出现在千万个房间里，这是人们第一次日常体验到共同收听。

abstract.en: A device named after invisible rays taught people to trust what they could hear but not see.
abstract.cn: 一台以看不见的射线命名的机器，教会人们去相信听得到却看不见的东西。

abstract.en: Radio silence is powerful because absence of signal is also a message.
abstract.cn: 无线电静默之所以有力，是因为没有信号本身也是一种消息。

examples.en: The radio on the shelf still works after forty years.
examples.cn: 架子上那台收音机用了四十年还能工作。

examples.en: Her talk will be broadcast on the radio this evening.
examples.cn: 她的谈话今晚将在广播中播出。

examples.en: The coast guard radioed the fishing boat to warn it of the storm.
examples.cn: 海岸警卫队用无线电通知渔船有暴风雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞迪欧」——声音不用电线，像射线一样飘进屋里，记住 radio 是收音机、无线电。

root: 拉丁语 radius（射线、辐条）→ radiare（发出射线）→ 科学构词成分 radi- → radiotelegraphy → 缩略为英语 radio；同族有 radar、radiation、radius。

sensesIntro.en: The core is signalling by rays; the senses divide into the receiving device, the broadcast service, the technology and the act of sending a message.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「靠射线传信」；义项分为接收设备、广播服务、技术本身，以及发送消息的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old radio's needle resting on a dial, its speaker faintly warm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台老式收音机的指针停在刻度盘上，扬声器微微发热。

branches.en: a dial turned by a thumb
branches.cn: 拇指转动的刻度盘

branches.en: a voice filling a kitchen
branches.cn: 填满厨房的一个声音

branches.en: an aerial on a ship's roof
branches.cn: 船顶的一根天线

branches.en: a message sent through fog
branches.cn: 穿过雾发出去的一条消息

branches.en: the same signal, once as a machine and once as a programme
branches.cn: 同一个信号，一次是机器，一次是节目

intro.en: The word is a modern shortening of a scientific compound built on the Latin stem for ray, with English endings for people and instruments.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「射线」词干上的科学复合词的现代缩略，加上表示人与器械的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem radi- is shared with radius and radiation, and it still builds new technical words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干 radi- 与 radius、radiation 共用，至今仍在构成新的技术词。

definition_zh: 铁轨；轨道；栏杆；扶手；铁路；怒斥
definition_en: one of the metal bars that a train runs on; a bar used for support or safety; the railway as a means of transport; to complain angrily
core_image: 一段刚抬到位的钢轨，卡进枕木上的扣件
scene: 站台上，工人把一段新钢轨抬到位，卡进枕木上的扣件。The workers laid a new section of rail along the curve.
sceneCN: 这里 rail 是「铁轨」（第 1 个义项：火车行驶其上的金属轨条）；句意为工人们沿着转弯处铺下了一段新的钢轨。画面里可留意：抬起的钢轨、枕木、扣件。

pos.zh: 铁轨；轨道；栏杆；扶手；铁路
怒斥；抱怨（多用于 rail against）

derivatives.zh: rail 加 -ing，指由栏杆组成的一排扶手或围栏
rail 与 way 复合，指铁路及其系统
rail 与 road 复合，美式用法，指铁路或铁路公司

senses.title: A metal bar for trains
senses.definition: one of the long metal bars on which a train's wheels run
senses.definitionCN: 火车车轮在其上行驶的长金属条之一
senses.example: The workers replaced a section of rail.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们更换了一段铁轨。
senses.why: The word comes from the Latin word for a straight rule, and a straight bar laid on the ground is exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语表示直尺的词，而铺在地上的一根直条正合此意。

senses.title: A bar for support or safety
senses.definition: a bar fixed along stairs or an edge to hold on to
senses.definitionCN: 沿楼梯或边缘固定、供人抓握的横杆
senses.example: Hold the rail as you go down the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 下台阶时抓住扶手。
senses.why: A straight bar serves equally as a track for wheels and as a handhold for people, so one word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 一根直杆既可为车轮当轨道，也可供人抓握，因此同一个词涵盖两者。

senses.title: The railway as transport
senses.definition: the railway system considered as a way of carrying people or goods
senses.definitionCN: 把人和货物运走的铁路系统
senses.example: They sent the goods by rail.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用铁路运送货物。
senses.why: By rail means by way of the rails, a common English habit of naming a transport system after its track.
senses.whyCN: by rail 意为经由铁路，这是英语常把交通系统以其轨道命名的习惯。

senses.title: To complain angrily
senses.definition: to speak angrily and at length about something, usually in rail against
senses.definitionCN: 对某事愤怒而冗长地发言，通常用于 rail against
senses.example: He railed against the new rules for ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他对着新规痛斥了十分钟。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different French word meaning to scold, and it happens to share the English spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来自另一个意为斥责的法语词，只是碰巧与 rail 共用同一个英语拼写。

intro.en: Rail comes from the Latin word for a straight rule, through French; the sense of scolding arrived separately from another French verb and merged in spelling.
intro.cn: rail 经法语来自拉丁语表示直尺的词；斥责义则另从一个法语动词而来，在拼写上合流。

items.en: Regula meant a straight stick or a rule, the tool used to test whether a line is straight.
items.cn: regula 指直棍或尺，是检验一条线是否笔直的工具。

items.en: Reille named a bar or a rail, and it also meant a rule in the sense of a standard.
items.cn: reille 指横杆或栏杆，也指作为标准的规则。

items.en: English rail first named a bar of wood or metal, then the bars laid for wagons and trains.
items.cn: 英语的 rail 先指木条或金属条，后指为货车与火车铺设的轨条。

items.en: The verb to rail, meaning to scold, came from a different French verb and took the same spelling.
items.cn: 表示斥责的动词 rail 来自另一个法语动词，却采用了相同的拼写。

items.en: Modern English uses rail for tracks, for handrails, for the railway itself and for angry complaint.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rail 指轨道、扶手、铁路本身，以及愤怒的抱怨。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same bar; the near-meaning group gathers words for tracks and supports.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一根「杆」构成的形式；近义组收表示轨道与支撑物的词。

entries.definition: A fence or barrier made of rails.
entries.definitionCN: 由横杆构成的围栏或护栏。

entries.definition: A track and system for trains.
entries.definitionCN: 供火车行驶的轨道与系统。

entries.definition: The American word for a railway.
To control by rules, from the same Latin word for a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 按规则控制，来自同一个表示尺与规则的拉丁词。

entries.definition: The pair of rails on which a train runs.
entries.definitionCN: 火车行驶其上的那对钢轨。

entries.definition: A long straight piece of metal or wood.
The handrail at the side of stairs.
The carrying of people or goods from place to place.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或货物从一处运到另一处。

normalIntro.en: The word is a straight bar: laid down it becomes a track, raised up it becomes a handrail, and joined together it becomes a railway.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一根直杆：铺下来是轨道，竖起来是扶手，连起来是铁路。

normal.en: Rail comes from the Latin word for a rule, which is also why regulate means to control by rules.
normal.cn: rail 来自拉丁语表示尺与规则的词，这也是 regulate 表示「按规则管理」的由来。

normal.en: By rail is the fixed phrase for travelling or sending goods by train.
normal.cn: by rail 是乘火车或经铁路运送货物的固定说法。

normal.en: A hand rail and a stair rail are the same bar, one for the hand and one for the stairs.
normal.cn: hand rail 与 stair rail 是同一根杆，一个供手抓，一个装在楼梯上。

normal.en: Railway is British, railroad is American, and both join rail to a word for a way.
normal.cn: railway 是英式，railroad 是美式，两者都把 rail 与表示「路」的词连在一起。

normal.en: To rail against something is to scold it at length, a sense that arrived from another French verb.
normal.cn: to rail against 某事物是长时间地斥责它，这一义项来自另一个法语动词。

abstract.en: A single straight bar becomes a whole system of movement once it is laid in a line, which is how infrastructure works.
abstract.cn: 一根直杆一旦被一线铺开，就成了整套运动系统，基础设施正是这样运作的。

abstract.en: A rail guides a train and a rail guards a stair: the same object either directs or protects.
abstract.cn: 铁轨引导火车，扶手保护走下楼梯的人：同一件东西要么引导，要么守护。

abstract.en: To rail against the world is to demand that it follow a straight rule, and the world rarely does.
abstract.cn: 对世界怒斥，就是要求它遵循一条笔直的规则，而世界很少如此。

examples.en: The train slowed as it crossed the rusty rail.
examples.cn: 火车越过那段生锈的铁轨时慢了下来。

examples.en: Please hold the rail while the floor is wet.
examples.cn: 地面湿滑时请抓住扶手。

examples.en: Most of the coal was carried by rail.
examples.cn: 大部分煤是通过铁路运输的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐欧」——一根锐利的直杆一直伸向远方，记住 rail 是铁轨、栏杆。

root: 拉丁语 regula（直尺、规则）→ 古法语 reille（横杆）→ 英语 rail；同族有 railing、railway、railroad、regulate。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a straight bar; the senses divide into a train track, a handhold, the railway system, and a separate verb of scolding.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一根直杆」；义项分为火车轨道、扶手、铁路系统，以及另出一个表示斥责的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a new steel rail lifted into place and clipped to the sleepers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段新钢轨被抬到位，扣在枕木上。

branches.en: wheels running along a bright line
branches.cn: 车轮沿一条亮线前行

branches.en: a hand gripping a stair rail
branches.cn: 握住楼梯扶手的一只手

branches.en: coal loaded into a long train
branches.cn: 装进长长列车的煤

branches.en: a voice scolding a notice board
branches.cn: 对着公告板斥责的声音

branches.en: the single bar and the system built from many
branches.cn: 单根轨条与由许多轨条组成的系统

intro.en: The word is a French borrowing on the Latin word for a rule, with English endings that build fences, systems and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「尺、规则」之上的法语借词，加上构成围栏、系统与复合词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin regula also gave English rule and regulate, which keep the sense of a straight standard.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regula 还给英语送来了 rule 与 regulate，它们保留了「笔直标准」的意思。

definition_zh: 铁路（英式）；铁路系统；铁路运输
definition_en: a track of rails with stations and signals, the usual British word for a railroad; the organization and system that runs trains; transport by train
core_image: 山谷里一座长满草旧车站，月台尽头立着褪色站牌
scene: 山谷里的旧车站已经长满草，月台尽头还立着一块褪色的站牌。The old railway once carried timber down the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 railway 是「铁路（英式说法）」（第 1 个义项：带车站与信号系统的轨道线路）；句意为这条旧铁路曾把木料运下山谷。画面里可留意：长草的月台、褪色站牌、通向谷底的轨线。

pos.zh: 铁路（英式）；铁路系统；铁路运输

derivatives.zh: railway 的第一成分，指单根轨条
美式对应词，指铁路或铁路公司
railway 与 man 复合，指铁路员工

senses.title: A track with stations and signals
senses.definition: a line of rails with its stations, signals and equipment, the usual British word for a railroad
senses.definitionCN: 带车站、信号与设备的轨道线路，英式英语对铁路的常用说法
senses.example: The old railway closed in the nineteen sixties.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧铁路在二十世纪六十年代停运了。
senses.why: British English joined rail and way to name the whole line, while American English chose rail and road.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语把 rail 与 way 组合起来命名整条线路，而美式英语选择了 rail 与 road。

senses.title: The organization and system
senses.definition: the body that owns the line and runs the trains
senses.definitionCN: 拥有线路并经营列车的机构
senses.example: She works for the national railway.
senses.exampleCN: 她在国家铁路部门工作。
senses.why: As with many networks, the physical line and the institution that operates it are called by one name.
senses.whyCN: 和许多网络一样，实体线路与运营它的机构共用一个名字。

senses.title: Transport by train
senses.definition: the carrying of people or goods by train, considered as a mode of transport
senses.definitionCN: 以火车运送人或货物，作为一种运输方式
senses.example: Goods moved by railway until the road was widened.
senses.exampleCN: 在公路拓宽之前，货物靠铁路运输。
senses.why: The system's name also names the service it provides, which is why people speak of sending something by railway.
senses.whyCN: 系统的名字也指它提供的服务，所以人们会说用铁路运送某物。

intro.en: Railway is a nineteenth-century English compound of rail and way, coined in Britain to name the new lines of track.
intro.cn: railway 是十九世纪的英语复合词，由 rail 与 way 组成，在英国被造出来命名新兴的轨道线路。

items.en: Rail came from the Latin word for a straight rule through French, and named the metal bar itself.
items.cn: rail 经法语来自拉丁语表示直尺的词，指的就是那根金属条。

items.en: Way is a native English word for a path or a route, older than any railway.
items.cn: way 是英语本族词，指路径或路线，比任何铁路都古老。

items.en: The compound railway named the way made of rails, a route built for locomotives.
items.cn: 复合词 railway 指由轨条铺成的路，为机车修建的路线。

items.en: British English kept railway for the line and the system, while American English settled on railroad.
items.cn: 英式英语保留 railway 指线路与系统，美式英语则固定用 railroad。

items.en: Modern English uses railway for the track, the company and the transport service, especially outside North America.
items.cn: 现代英语用 railway 指轨道、公司与运输服务，尤其在北美以外。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same compound; the near-meaning group gathers words for rail systems and routes.
note.cn: 形近组收同一复合词的形式；近义组收表示铁路系统与路线的词。

entries.definition: The American word for the same system.
A single metal bar for wheels.
entries.definitionCN: 供车轮行驶的一根金属条。

entries.definition: A person employed by a railway.
A single route of track between places.
entries.definitionCN: 两地之间的一条轨道线路。

entries.definition: A route of track or wire between places.
entries.definitionCN: 两地之间的轨道或线路。

entries.definition: The pair of rails a train runs on.
entries.definitionCN: 火车行驶其上的那对钢轨。

entries.definition: A set of connected routes.
The carrying of people or goods.

normalIntro.en: The word is rail plus way, the British way of naming a road of rails; the American cousin is railroad.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 rail 加 way，是英式命名「轨条之路」的方式；它的美国亲戚是 railroad。

normal.en: Railway is rail plus way, railroad is rail plus road: two languages, one idea.
normal.cn: railway 是 rail 加 way，railroad 是 rail 加 road：两种语言，同一个想法。

normal.en: A railway station is where the line meets the town, and a railway carriage is one coach on it.
normal.cn: railway station 是线路与城镇相接之处，railway carriage 是线上的一节车厢。

normal.en: The national railway is the publicly owned system, as opposed to a private company.
normal.cn: the national railway 指公有的铁路系统，与私营公司相对。

normal.en: By railway is less common than by rail, which is the usual short phrase.
normal.cn: by railway 不如 by rail 常用，后者才是通常的简短说法。

normal.en: A railwayman works on the line, a word that survives mainly in British writing.
normal.cn: railwayman 指在铁路上工作的人，这个词主要保留在英式书面语里。

abstract.en: A railway is a promise that the same route will be there tomorrow, which is why it changed how people planned their lives.
abstract.cn: 铁路是一种承诺：同一条路线明天仍在那里，因此它改变了人们安排生活的方式。

abstract.en: Cutting a railway through a valley is an act that both connects and divides the land.
abstract.cn: 在山谷里修一条铁路，既连接也分割了这片土地。

abstract.en: When a railway closes, the towns along it quietly become places people pass by instead of stop at.
abstract.cn: 一条铁路停运后，沿线的城镇悄然变成人们经过而不再停留的地方。

examples.en: The railway between the two towns was built in eighteen fifty.
examples.cn: 两镇之间的铁路建于1850年。

examples.en: He found work on the railway after the mill closed.
examples.cn: 磨坊关闭后，他在铁路部门找到了工作。

examples.en: Timber was carried by railway until the road was improved.
examples.cn: 在公路改善之前，木料靠铁路运输。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐欧威」——轨条铺成一条路，向远方延伸，记住 railway 是铁路。

root: rail（轨条，源自拉丁语 regula）+ way（路，英语本族词）复合而成，十九世纪出现；同族有 railroad、railwayman。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a way of rails; the senses divide into the British railway line, the system that runs it, and transport by train.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「由轨条铺成的路」；义项分为英式铁路线路、运营它的系统，以及铁路运输。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an overgrown station in a valley, a faded sign at the platform's end.
core.cn: 核心意象：山谷里长满草的旧车站，月台尽头一块褪色的站牌。

branches.en: a track disappearing into a valley
branches.cn: 没入山谷的一条轨道

branches.en: a timetable in a station office
branches.cn: 车站办公室里的时刻表

branches.en: timber stacked on a flat wagon
branches.cn: 堆在平板车上的木料

branches.en: rails rusting under long grass
branches.cn: 在深草下生锈的轨条

branches.en: the same line, once busy and once abandoned
branches.cn: 同一条线路，一次繁忙，一次废弃

intro.en: The compound joins a Latin-derived rail to a native way, and English endings extend it to workers and to individual lines.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把源自拉丁语的 rail 与本族的 way 结合，英语词尾又把它扩展到工作者与单条线路。

latinIntro.en: Only rail has a Latin source, the word for a straight rule.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 rail 有拉丁语来源，即表示直尺的词。

items.meaning: a stopping place on a line

definition_zh: 雨；雨水；下雨；如雨般落下
definition_en: water that falls from clouds in drops; to fall as rain; a large number of things falling or arriving at once
core_image: 屋檐下连成一线落下的水珠
scene: 早晨的街道上，行人撑起伞，水沿着屋檐一线线落下。The rain kept the whole village indoors for two days.
sceneCN: 这里 rain 是「雨」（第 1 个义项：从云中落下的水滴）；句意为这场雨让整个村子两天都待在室内。画面里可留意：伞面、屋檐滴落的水线、空荡的街道。

pos.zh: 雨；雨水；一阵如雨之物
下雨；如雨般落下

derivatives.zh: rain 加 -y，指多雨的、下雨的
rain 与 fall 复合，指一段时间内的降雨量
rain 与 coat 复合，指防雨的外套

senses.title: Water falling from clouds
senses.definition: water that falls from clouds in drops and reaches the ground
senses.definitionCN: 从云中以水滴形式落下并到达地面的水
senses.example: The rain lasted all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这场雨下了一整个上午。
senses.why: Old English regn named the falling water directly, and the word has stayed close to the weather ever since.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 regn 直接命名这种落下的水，此后这个词一直紧贴天气这一含义。

senses.title: To fall as rain
senses.definition: to fall from the sky as drops of water, used of the weather itself
senses.definitionCN: 以水滴形式从天空落下，用于描述天气本身
senses.example: It rained for three days without stopping.
senses.exampleCN: 雨连下了三天没停。
senses.why: The noun became an impersonal verb, so English can say it rains without naming who or what is acting.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了无人称动词，因此英语可以说 it rains，而不必指出动作的执行者。

senses.title: A great number falling at once
senses.definition: a large number of things coming down or arriving together, as if falling like drops
senses.definitionCN: 大量事物像水滴一样同时落下或到来
senses.example: A rain of stones fell from the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵石块从崖上落下。
senses.why: Because rain is countless drops arriving together, the word became a picture for anything that comes in a shower.
senses.whyCN: 雨是无数水滴一同到来，因此这个词成了任何「成阵而至」之物的画面。

intro.en: Rain is a native English word from Old English regn, with relatives in other Germanic languages; no Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: rain 是英语本族词，来自古英语 regn，在其他日耳曼语言中有亲属词；没有拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Regn meant rain, and it was used in compounds for storms and wet weather.
items.cn: regn 意为雨，也用于构成表示风暴与潮湿天气的复合词。

items.en: The word is reconstructed in older Germanic with the same sense, and related forms appear across northern Europe.
items.cn: 这个词在更早的日耳曼语中被重构为同样的意思，相关形式遍布北欧。

items.en: Middle English rain kept the spelling close to the old form while the verb rained developed beside it.
items.cn: 中古英语的 rain 拼写接近古形，同时发展出动词 rained。

items.en: Rain combined with fall and coat to name what rain does and what protects against it.
items.cn: rain 与 fall、coat 组合，命名雨的作用以及防雨之物。

items.en: Modern English uses rain for the water, the weather, and figuratively for anything arriving in quantity.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rain 指水、天气，并比喻任何大量到来之物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and one homophone; the near-meaning group gathers words for falling water.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词与一个同音词；近义组收表示落水的词。

entries.definition: Having a lot of rain.
The amount of rain that falls in a period.
A coat that keeps rain out.
The period during which a monarch rules, a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 君主统治的时期，同音但不同源。

entries.definition: A short fall of rain.
A very heavy fall of rain.
Light rain falling in fine drops.
entries.definitionCN: 以细小雨滴落下的毛毛雨。

entries.definition: Water that falls from clouds as rain, snow or hail.
entries.definitionCN: 以雨、雪或冰雹形式从云中落下的水。

normalIntro.en: The word names the falling water, then the weather, then anything that arrives like drops in a shower.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词先命名落下的水，再指天气，最后指任何像水滴一样成阵而至的东西。

normal.en: Rain and reign sound the same, but one falls from the sky while the other is held by a monarch.
normal.cn: rain 与 reign 同音，但一个从天上落下，一个由君主掌握。

normal.en: Rainy is the adjective, rainfall is the measured amount, and raincoat is the thing you wear.
normal.cn: rainy 是形容词，rainfall 是测得的雨量，raincoat 是穿在身上的东西。

normal.en: It rained is impersonal: the it does not point to anyone, because weather has no actor.
normal.cn: it rained 是无人称句：it 不指向任何人，因为天气没有执行者。

normal.en: Rain or shine is the phrase for doing something whatever the weather.
normal.cn: rain or shine 是无论天气如何都要做某事的说法。

normal.en: A rain of stones uses the weather word for anything falling in great numbers.
normal.cn: a rain of stones 用天气词指大量落下的任何东西。

abstract.en: Rain is the most ordinary proof that something can arrive without being invited.
abstract.cn: 雨是「事物会不请自来」这件事最平常的证明。

abstract.en: Farmers read rain as promise or threat, which shows how one word can carry both hope and fear.
abstract.cn: 农民把雨读成许诺或威胁，可见同一个词能同时承载希望与恐惧。

abstract.en: A rain of stones and a rain of questions share the word because both overwhelm by number.
abstract.cn: 石雨与问题雨共用一个词，因为两者都以数量压倒了人。

examples.en: The rain stopped just before the match began.
examples.cn: 比赛开始前雨刚好停了。

examples.en: It rained so hard that the road disappeared under water.
examples.cn: 雨下得太大，路面被水淹没了。

examples.en: A rain of small stones rattled on the roof.
examples.cn: 一阵小石块噼里啪啦打在屋顶上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞恩」——天上落下的水滴一颗颗，记住 rain 是雨、下雨。

root: 古英语 regn（雨）→ 中古英语 rain → 现代英语 rain；同族有 rainy、rainfall、raincoat。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is falling water; the senses divide into the water itself, the weather, and anything arriving in a shower.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「落下的水」；义项分为水本身、天气，以及任何成阵而至之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: drops falling in a continuous line from the edge of a roof.
core.cn: 核心意象：水珠从屋檐边连成一线落下。

branches.en: an empty street under umbrellas
branches.cn: 伞下空荡的街道

branches.en: a window grey with weather
branches.cn: 被天气染灰的窗

branches.en: stones rattling down a cliff
branches.cn: 从崖上滚落的石块

branches.en: the same falling, once as water and once as stones
branches.cn: 同一种下落，一次是水，一次是石头

branches.en: weather that arrives and things that arrive in numbers
branches.cn: 到来的天气与成批到来的东西

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its family is built from English compounds and a simple adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是本族短词，其词族由英语复合词与一个简单的形容词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语同族词记录。

definition_zh: 举起；提高；筹集；抚养；提出；引起
definition_en: to lift something to a higher position; to increase an amount or level; to collect money for a purpose; to bring up children or animals; to put a subject forward for discussion; to cause a feeling or reaction
core_image: 一只举到半空的手，掌心朝前
scene: 会议室里，一位成员把手举到半空，示意想就预算发问。She raised her hand and waited for the chair to notice her.
sceneCN: 这里 raise 是「举起」（第 1 个义项：把某物抬到更高的位置）；句意为她举起手，等主席注意到她。画面里可留意：举到半空的手、朝前的手掌、会议桌。

pos.zh: 举起；提高；筹集；抚养；提出；引起
加薪（美式）；提高

derivatives.zh: raise 加 -er，指筹集者或饲养者
raise 加 -ing，指举起、抚养或筹集的过程
fund 与 raiser 复合，指筹款活动或筹款人

senses.title: To lift to a higher position
senses.definition: to move something upward to a higher place or level
senses.definitionCN: 把某物向上移到更高的位置或水平
senses.example: Raise your hand if you have a question.
senses.exampleCN: 有问题请举手。
senses.why: The word came into English from Old Norse with the plain sense of setting something upright or lifting it, and that physical act is still the centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从古诺斯语进入英语，本义是把某物立起或抬起，这个身体动作至今仍是核心。

senses.title: To increase an amount
senses.definition: to make a price, level or amount higher
senses.definitionCN: 使价格、水平或数量变高
senses.example: The shop raised its prices twice this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店今年两次提价。
senses.why: Raising a thing higher and raising a number higher use the same image, so the word moved easily from objects to quantities.
senses.whyCN: 把东西举高与把数字提高用的是同一幅画面，所以这个词从实物轻易地转向了数量。

senses.title: To collect money
senses.definition: to gather money or support for a purpose, often for charity
senses.definitionCN: 为某个目的募集钱款或支持，常指慈善
senses.example: The class raised money for the animal shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 全班为动物收容所筹集了钱款。
senses.why: Money that is brought together and lifted into a common fund looks like something raised up from many hands.
senses.whyCN: 把分散的钱聚拢并抬进一个共同基金，看起来就像从许多只手中把东西举起来。

senses.title: To bring up children or animals
senses.definition: to care for a child or an animal until it is grown
senses.definitionCN: 照料孩子或动物直到长大
senses.example: She raised three children on her own.
senses.exampleCN: 她独自抚养了三个孩子。
senses.why: To raise a child is to lift that person up through years of care, and the same verb serves for animals on a farm.
senses.whyCN: 抚养孩子就是通过多年照料把人「托举」起来，同一个动词也用于农场里的动物。

senses.title: To put a subject forward
senses.definition: to bring a question or subject to other people's attention for discussion
senses.definitionCN: 把问题或话题提到别人面前供讨论
senses.example: He raised a question about the schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 他就日程安排提了一个问题。
senses.why: A subject brought into a conversation is lifted into view, so the word of lifting also means to mention for discussion.
senses.whyCN: 被带进对话的话题被举到众人眼前，于是「举起」这个词也指提出来讨论。

senses.title: To cause a feeling or reaction
senses.definition: to produce a feeling, doubt or reaction in people
senses.definitionCN: 在人们心中产生某种感受、疑虑或反应
senses.example: The news raised fears of another delay.
senses.exampleCN: 这则消息引起了对再次延误的担忧。
senses.why: If an action lifts a feeling into notice, it causes that feeling, and this sense extends the word from things to emotions.
senses.whyCN: 一个举动把某种情绪举到众人注意之中，就是引起了那种情绪，这一义项把词从实物扩展到情感。

intro.en: Raise came into English from Old Norse, where the verb meant to set something upright; it is related to rise but carries an object.
intro.cn: raise 从古诺斯语进入英语，那个动词意为把某物立起；它与 rise 相关，但必须带宾语。

items.en: Reisa meant to raise or to set upright, and Norse settlers brought it into northern English.
items.cn: reisa 意为举起或立起，诺斯定居者把它带入英格兰北部。

items.en: Raise and rise come from the same family, but rise is what a thing does and raise is what someone does to it.
items.cn: raise 与 rise 同属一族，但 rise 是事物自身发生的动作，raise 是某人对它施加的动作。

items.en: Middle English raise kept the sense of lifting and setting up, and added the sense of bringing up a child.
items.cn: 中古英语的 raise 保留了举起与竖立的意思，并增加了抚养孩子的义项。

items.en: From lifting objects came lifting prices, collecting money, raising a subject and raising a feeling.
items.cn: 从举物生出提价、筹钱、提出话题与引起情绪等义。

items.en: Modern English uses raise for lifting, increasing, collecting, nurturing, mentioning and causing, and as a noun for a pay increase.
items.cn: 现代英语用 raise 表示举起、增加、筹集、养育、提及与引起，并作名词指加薪。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of lifting and increasing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根上的形式；近义组收表示举起与增加的动词。

entries.definition: To go upward by itself, without an object.
entries.definitionCN: 自身向上移动，不带宾语。

entries.definition: To begin to exist, especially of a problem.
A person or thing that raises.
The act of lifting, collecting or bringing up.
entries.definitionCN: 举起、筹集或抚养的行为。

entries.definition: To move something upward with effort.
entries.definitionCN: 费力地把某物向上移动。

entries.definition: To make or become larger in amount.
To gather things or money together.
To care for someone while they grow.
entries.definitionCN: 在某人成长过程中给予照料。

normalIntro.en: The word always needs an object: someone raises something, whether a hand, a price, money, a child, a question or a fear.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词总要带宾语：某人把某样东西举起，无论是手、价格、钱款、孩子、问题还是恐惧。

normal.en: Raise needs an object and rise does not: you raise your hand, but the sun rises.
normal.cn: raise 需要宾语而 rise 不需要：你举起手，而太阳自己升起。

normal.en: A pay raise in American English is what British English calls a pay rise.
normal.cn: 美式英语的 a pay raise 就是英式英语的 a pay rise。

normal.en: Raise money means collect it, while raise prices means increase them: the same verb, two directions of lift.
normal.cn: raise money 是筹集，raise prices 是提高：同一个动词，两种「抬升」方向。

normal.en: Raise children and raise animals both mean care for them until grown.
normal.cn: raise children 与 raise animals 都指照料其长大。

normal.en: Raise a question is to bring it up, not to answer it.
normal.cn: raise a question 是把问题提出来，而不是回答它。

abstract.en: Almost everything people do to improve a situation can be said with this one verb, which is why it appears so often in meetings.
abstract.cn: 人们为改善处境所做的几乎每件事都能用这一个动词表达，所以它在会议里出现得如此频繁。

abstract.en: To raise a child is to lift someone you cannot fully control, and that is the daily risk of parenting.
abstract.cn: 抚养孩子就是托举一个你无法完全掌控的人，这正是养育的日常风险。

abstract.en: A question raised is a question someone must now carry, even if nobody answers it.
abstract.cn: 一个被提出的问题，就成了某人必须背负的问题，即使没有人回答。

examples.en: He raised the box above his head and held it there.
examples.cn: 他把箱子举过头顶，稳稳停在那里。

examples.en: The government plans to raise the minimum wage next year.
examples.cn: 政府计划明年提高最低工资。

examples.en: They raised enough money to rebuild the bridge.
examples.cn: 他们筹到了足够的钱重建那座桥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞兹」——把东西锐利地向上托起，记住 raise 是举起、提高。

root: 古诺斯语 reisa（举起、立起）→ 中古英语 raise → 现代英语 raise；与 rise、arise 同族。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an upward lift; the senses divide into lifting an object, raising a number, collecting money, bringing up the young, putting a subject forward and causing a feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「向上托举」；义项分为举起实物、提高数字、筹集钱款、养育幼小、提出话题与引起情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifted into the air, palm forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举到半空、掌心朝前的手。

branches.en: a box held above the head
branches.cn: 举过头顶的一只箱子

branches.en: a price tag rewritten higher
branches.cn: 被改写成更高数字的价签

branches.en: coins gathered from many hands
branches.cn: 从许多只手里聚拢的硬币

branches.en: a child guided step by step
branches.cn: 一步步被引导的孩子

branches.en: the same lift applied to a question and to a fear
branches.cn: 同一种抬升，一次用于问题，一次用于恐惧

intro.en: The word is a Norse borrowing, and English built its relatives with an agent suffix and a participle rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: 这个词是古诺斯语借词，英语用施动者词尾与分词来构成亲属词，而非拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语同族词记录。

definition_zh: 范围；幅度；射程；山脉；在…范围内变动；靶场
definition_en: a set of different things of the same type; the limits within which something varies; the distance a weapon or signal can reach; a line of connected mountains; to vary between two limits; a place for shooting practice
core_image: 一把拉伸开的软尺，刻度从这头排到那头
scene: 清晨的靶场里，射手把标尺架好，远处的山脊像一条长线铺到天边。The rifle had a range of nearly a thousand metres.
sceneCN: 这里 range 是「射程」（第 3 个义项：武器能打到的距离）；句意为这支步枪的射程接近一千米。画面里可留意：架起的标尺、远处的山脊、靶场尽头的靶子。

pos.zh: 范围；幅度；射程；山脉；靶场
在…范围内变动；排列

derivatives.zh: range 加前缀 a-，指按次序摆放、安排

senses.title: A set of varieties
senses.definition: a set of different things of the same type, or the limits within which something varies
senses.definitionCN: 同类事物的一个系列，或某物变动的限度
senses.example: The shop sells a wide range of teas.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售种类繁多的茶。
senses.why: From a row of things laid out in order came the idea of a whole series of varieties under one name.
senses.whyCN: 从「按次序排开的一行」生出「同类事物构成的一整个系列」这一概念。

senses.title: A line of mountains
senses.definition: a series of connected hills or mountains forming a long line
senses.definitionCN: 连成一条长线的一串丘陵或山峰
senses.example: A mountain range runs along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 一条山脉沿着边境延伸。
senses.why: Mountains seen from a distance stand in a long row, so the row word was applied to them directly.
senses.whyCN: 远望群山时它们排成长长一行，于是这个「行」的词被直接用在山上。

senses.title: The distance a weapon reaches
senses.definition: the distance over which a gun, missile or signal can reach its target
senses.definitionCN: 枪、导弹或信号能够到达目标的距离
senses.example: The rifle had a range of nearly a thousand metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这支步枪的射程接近一千米。
senses.why: Gunners measured how far a shot could travel, and that measured extent was called its range.
senses.whyCN: 炮手会测量一发炮弹能飞多远，这段被测出的距离就称作它的 range。

senses.title: To vary between limits
senses.definition: to vary between two fixed limits, used of prices, sizes, temperatures and the like
senses.definitionCN: 在两个固定限度之间变动，用于价格、尺寸、温度等
senses.example: Temperatures range from ten to thirty degrees here.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的气温在十到三十度之间变动。
senses.why: Once range named the limits themselves, the verb could describe anything moving between them.
senses.whyCN: range 一旦指限度本身，动词便可用来说明任何在限度之间移动的事物。

senses.title: A place for shooting practice
senses.definition: an area laid out with targets where people practise shooting
senses.definitionCN: 排布着靶子、供人练习射击的场地
senses.example: The recruits spent the morning at the shooting range.
senses.exampleCN: 新兵们在射击场度过了一个上午。
senses.why: A range is also a measured stretch of ground, and a shooting ground is exactly that: a marked extent with targets.
senses.whyCN: range 也指一段测好的地面，而射击场正是如此：一片标好的、设有靶子的场地。

intro.en: Range comes from Old French range, a row or line, probably from a Frankish word for a ring of men; all its senses grew from the idea of things set out in order.
intro.cn: range 来自古法语 range（一行、一列），可能源自法兰克语中表示一圈人的词；所有义项都从「按次序排开」这一想法生长出来。

items.en: Old French range meant a row or line, and it named things placed in order.
items.cn: 古法语 range 意为一行或一列，用来命名按次序摆放的东西。

items.en: The word is traced to a Frankish term for a ring or band of men, which gave the idea of a line.
items.cn: 这个词可追溯到法兰克语中表示一圈或一队人的词，由此产生「一行」的概念。

items.en: Middle English used range for a row and a rank, and then for the extent something could cover.
items.cn: 中古英语用 range 指一排、一列，随后又指某物所能覆盖的范围。

items.en: Gunners spoke of the range of a shot, and the word became the measured distance a weapon could reach.
items.cn: 炮手们会说一发炮弹的 range，这个词便成了武器能到达的实测距离。

items.en: Modern English extends range to mountains, to variation between limits, and to grounds for shooting practice.
items.cn: 现代英语把 range 扩展到山脉、限度之间的变动，以及练习射击的场地。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same row-and-line idea; the near-meaning group gathers words for extent and distance.
note.cn: 形近组收基于同一「排列成行」概念构成的词；近义组收表示范围与距离的词。

entries.definition: To put things in a particular order.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物按特定次序摆放。

entries.definition: The way things are put in order.
A person who patrols and protects a wild area.
A row or a position in order, a related Germanic word.
entries.definitionCN: 一行或在次序中的位置，相关的日耳曼词。

entries.definition: The area or degree that something covers.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所覆盖的面积或程度。

entries.definition: The range of what something deals with.
The distance or time from one end to the other.
entries.definitionCN: 从一端到另一端的距离或时间。

entries.definition: The space between two points.

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a row, then widens into a series, a reachable distance, a line of hills, a spread of values and a marked ground.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从一行开始，逐步扩展为系列、可达的距离、连绵的山、数值的跨度，以及标好的场地。

normal.en: Range and arrange share the same old row, one naming the line and the other the act of setting it out.
normal.cn: range 与 arrange 共享同一个古老的「行」，一个命名这条线，一个命名把线排开的行为。

normal.en: A mountain range is simply mountains standing in a long row.
normal.cn: 一条 mountain range 就是排成长长一行的山。

normal.en: A rifle's range is how far its shot can travel before it falls.
normal.cn: 步枪的 range 是子弹在落下之前能飞多远。

normal.en: When prices range from low to high, they vary between two limits.
normal.cn: 当价格 range from low to high，它们就在两个限度之间变动。

normal.en: A shooting range is a field laid out with targets for practice.
normal.cn: shooting range 是排好靶子供练习的场地。

abstract.en: Range names the space between a starting point and a limit, whether in distance, price or ability.
abstract.cn: range 是「起点与限度之间的空间」这个词，无论那空间在距离、价格还是能力上。

abstract.en: To say something is out of range is to say it lies beyond where your reach stops.
abstract.cn: 说某物 out of range，就是说它落在你触及范围的边界之外。

abstract.en: A wide range is not just many things but many things set side by side in order.
abstract.cn: a wide range 不只是许多东西，而是许多东西按次序并排摆开。

examples.en: The shop sells a wide range of teas.
examples.cn: 这家店出售种类繁多的茶。

examples.en: The missile has a range of over two thousand kilometres.
examples.cn: 这种导弹的射程超过两千公里。

examples.en: Temperatures range from ten to thirty degrees here.
examples.cn: 这里的气温在十到三十度之间变动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「软尺」——把软尺拉开来量，从这头到那头都是范围，记住 range 是范围、射程、山脉。

root: 古法语 range（一行、一列）→ 中古英语 range → 现代英语 range；可能与法兰克语「一圈人」有关。同族有 arrange、arrangement、ranger。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a row laid out in order; the senses move from a series of varieties to a line of mountains, the reach of a weapon, variation between limits and a shooting ground.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是按次序排开的一行；义项从同类系列，到山脉，再到武器可达的距离、限度之间的变动，以及射击场地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft measuring tape stretched out, its marks running in a straight row.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把拉伸开的软尺，刻度排成笔直的一行。

branches.en: a shelf of bottles lined up in a row
branches.cn: 一排摆开的瓶子

branches.en: ridges running to the horizon
branches.cn: 延伸至地平线的山脊

branches.en: a marked distance on a rifle sight
branches.cn: 步枪准星上标出的距离

branches.en: a thermometer rising and falling
branches.cn: 上下浮动的温度计

branches.en: targets standing at the far end of a field
branches.cn: 立在场地尽头的靶子

intro.en: The word is a borrowing from Old French, and its family is built with English prefixes, suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词借自古法语，其词族由英语前缀、后缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word; the older root is Frankish.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录；更早的词根是法兰克语。
